description:
A proven binary is read inline: byte_size, bit_size, ==, a whole rest at position 0, and a small aligned slice.

Today:
- byte_size is a 23-instruction extern (fz_bitstring_byte_extent, lib/kernel.fz:1308, ir_runtime.rs:1065) for about 6 instructions of work, and it is not folded for a literal: 49 instructions to compute a constant (M3, C8, JSON proposal P2).
- Binary == takes fz_value_eq_widening_ref (prim.rs:1936-1952): AnyValue round trips, a schema RefCell borrow, no length early-out, and 10 instructions turning the C bool into an atom and back. Equal and different both cost ~500. a == "true" costs 385, while case a do "true" is ~34 inline (M4, C10).
- A whole-rest read always calls fz_bs_read_binary_ref (prim.rs:880-899), even at the constant position 0, where the runtime returns the source anyway after 158 instructions (M7a).
- A 4 B slice costs 653 instructions. The extern recomputes the field_end the caller proved (BitFieldFits) (M11).

Fix: on lanes proven binary, emit the decode inline (the match code already has it):
- byte_size/bit_size inline; literals folded.
- A binary == arm: length compare, pointer shortcut, memcmp (or one small extern on ptr/len). The result is a condition, so no atom. a == literal reuses the inline literal compare that matching already emits.
- Whole rest at position 0 is the source.
- Small aligned slices are inline, with no re-validation (debug_assert only).

What goes away: byte_extent as a call, the binary path through the widening eq, field_end re-validation, and fz_bs_read_* recomputing ends (R5).

Asm first: target listings from the probes child, for p02a/b/c, p07a/b/c/e, p03c and p08. Predictions are written before building:
- byte_size ~30 (after the share child) and the literal folded
- == under 100
- the accumulator loop with a later byte_size: 448 -> 279
Judged on bench.
title: A proven binary is read inline: byte_size, ==, whole rest, small slice
